assessment: The actual wrapper entrypoint invokes the shared refusal_exit_boundary. A result defaults to125 and is replaced only after main returns an integer; outer finally selects self_exit when refusal is present on normal return, invalid result or an exception. No diagnostic I/O precedes that final self-exit selection.

The predicate checks both the explicit refusal flag and globally retained active Authority, so an exception before the old flag assignment still observes sticky refusal. The actual Popen is held globally immediately after creation, before signal-unmask and later evidence handling.

Therefore a later stdout.close or diagnostic-write exception cannot bypass this boundary and fall through to ordinary interpreter finalization when sticky refusal is set. Permission refusal remains unresolved; this is not a new clean-custody claim.

The new sixth no-process check calls the actual shared boundary with retained synthetic child and refused authority. Both close and diagnostic exceptional-tail variants require exit125 selection, child retention, no ordinary-finalization/process callback and unresolved custody. The injected self-exit callback raises its own sentinel; it executes no os._exit or native child.

Final diagnostic delivery encodes at most65536 output bytes, uses a nonblocking descriptor and a50ms deadline further capped by cleanup_deadline_ns. Write/close failures may still interrupt evidence handling, but the outer refusal boundary now covers them; absent or failed evidence cannot qualify a clean result.
